issues.description: extract_arch_from_url returns None on regex miss and the caller interpolates 'None' into the constructed URL.
issues.detail: When the arch regex fails to match, the function silently returns None, and use_koji_url_only embeds it directly into an f-string, producing '/latest/None/Packages' as a malformed URL that surfaces as a 404 far from the cause. Either raise on failure or have the caller check and reject explicitly.

issues.description: nevra[0] indexes the filename's first character rather than the package name's first letter, with no stated precondition.
issues.detail: The koji Packages tree is keyed by the lowercased first letter of the package NAME, but the code takes the first character of the basename of the URL. It happens to coincide for typical inputs, but the precondition (URL basename equals a NEVRA-shaped RPM filename starting with the package name) is asserted nowhere. Name the variable filename and compute the package name explicitly.

issues.description: use_koji_url_only lacks a stated contract for inputs and outputs.
issues.detail: The function assumes every non-pool URL contains a recognized arch token and a NEVRA-shaped filename, but neither precondition nor postcondition is documented. The race condition acknowledged in the PR description (URLs crafted before coreos-koji-tagger tags) is also an unstated invariant that should at minimum live in a module docstring so future callers don't reuse the function unsafely.

issues.description: Arch regex is fragile and may misclassify URLs whose path contains an arch substring before the real arch.
issues.detail: search() returns the first match, so a path like '.../ppc64le-mirror/.../x86_64/Packages/...' yields the wrong arch. The regex is also heavier than needed for a four-element list — split on '/' and intersect with an ARCHES set, or thread the arch in from the caller which already knows it. noarch is also a legal arch that's unhandled.

issues.description: Koji URL base, arch list, and path layout are scattered string literals without a single source of truth.
issues.detail: The arch list inside extract_arch_from_url is independent of the arches the caller iterates over, and the canonical koji path layout is inlined as string concatenation. Lift the arches to a module-level ARCHES constant and extract a build_koji_url(nevra, arch) helper so the koji contract lives in one place.

issues.description: Coreos-pool prioritization in query_packages_location is now redundant with use_koji_url_only and should be removed or justified.
issues.detail: The new pass rewrites every URL into the canonical koji form, making the earlier 'prioritize the URL from fedora-coreos-pool' branch dead work. Two filters doing the same job is worse than one — either delete the prioritization or add a comment explaining why it remains load-bearing.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a workable but under-specified patch. Two concrete defects dominate: extract_arch_from_url can return None and the caller silently embeds it as the literal string 'None' in a constructed URL, and nevra[0] reads the filename's first character rather than the package name's first letter without stating the precondition that makes them coincide. The arch regex is also fragile (substring misclassification, no noarch support) and heavier than the n=4 data warrants. Contracts for use_koji_url_only — including the acknowledged tagging race — are nowhere stated, and the coreos-pool prioritization in query_packages_location is now redundant. Fix the None path and the variable naming before merge; tighten the module boundary soon after.
